title: Maintenance window ops notes: driver pairing and SLA wedge (2026-05)
content:
Purpose
This doc captures the informal run notes for the upcoming driver upgrade/firmware maintenance that touches kernel modules and NVIDIA driver stack. Focus is on: pairing nodes for minimal impact, defining a temporary SLA "wedge" we can tolerate during rolling upgrades, and concrete pre/post checks to avoid surprises. This is an ops working doc (not the official runbook).

Context and constraints
- Upgrade required to land security patch + new CUDA kernels needed by the 70B performance pack.
- Hardware mix: A100s (64GB) in us-west1/us-east1; H100 in eu-west1 for dedicated pools.
- We must keep the hosted tier at >= 98.5% availability during business hours. The SRE + infra target for the maintenance windows is to keep 95th latency within 1x baseline and 99th within 1.5x baseline.
- We will adopt a "SLA wedge" concept: allow a controlled, short-lived drop in SLA for certain non-critical placement pools (dev/burst). Critical customers on Dedicated should be routed to reserved capacity and not touched where possible.

Strategy summary
1) Pairing-first approach: rather than evacuating an entire rack or AZ at once, pick node-pairs (pair = two servers sharing the same NVLink fabric) and upgrade the driver on one node of the pair while keeping its partner in service to host hot KV caches. After validation, upgrade the second node. This reduces cache warmup and cold-start tail events.
2) Stagger windows by region and traffic pattern: eu-west1 first during US daytime to catch issues early; then us-west1; then us-east1; finally ap-southeast1 (minimal regional load expected).
3) Precomputed fallbacks: create model fallbacks (smaller quantized variant) and routing rules that can be activated per-route if tail latency or error rate exceeds thresholds.

Planned windows (initial cadence) 
- eu-west1 (pilot): 2026-05-17 01:00-05:00 UTC (local: 02:00-06:00 BST) — 8 node-pairs, expected 12% capacity removed at any time.
- us-west1 (main): 2026-05-18 03:00-09:00 UTC (local: 20:00-02:00 PDT) — rolling 6-hour window per colo, maximum 18% capacity reduction per colo.
- us-east1 (secondary): 2026-05-19 02:00-08:00 UTC — lower traffic window, max 15% capacity reduction.
- ap-southeast1 (low impact): 2026-05-21 22:00-04:00 UTC — 6% capacity reduction target.

Region capacity snapshot (pre-maintenance)
- eu-west1: 320 GPUs total; 64 GPUs in the dedicated pool used by enterprise customers (pinning excluded).
- us-west1: 560 GPUs total; 140 GPUs reserved for Dedicated.
- us-east1: 480 GPUs total; 120 GPUs reserved.
- ap-southeast1: 120 GPUs total; 24 GPUs reserved.
Expected removal is always from non-reserved pools first. Numbers above are used to compute percent impact in the pilot.

Impact assumptions and metrics to watch
- Expected queue length increase: +35% for short windows on affected pools (paired approach).
- Expected P95 token latency increase: up to +30% on spike if cache warmups happen.
- Error rate threshold to abort window: continuous 2.5%+ 5xxs over 10 minutes OR spike in client-side retries > 3x baseline.
- Fallback activation threshold: 95th latency > 1.5x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes for any model route.
- Auto-throttle: if ingress token rate falls by >20% (client-side holiday), we can accelerate pairing.

Pre-window checklist (owners in parens)
- Validate canary on isolated test pool (Diego) — run 1000 sample requests against quantized and non-quantized kernels.
- Snapshot KV caches for top-5 cached prefixes (SRE) — ensure we can pre-warm key sets on partner nodes.
- Confirm Dedicated customer routing rules (Product + Customer Success) — list customers that must not be touched.
- Prepare roll-forward and rollback artifacts: kernel modules, driver bundle hash, rollback playbook PR (GitHub PR #902).
- Notify customers: 72h + 24h notices and a reminder 1h before start (Customer Success).

Operational steps (high level)
1) Outbound notice and page duty roster check. Confirm on-call SRE and infra for region.
2) Mark selected node-pair targets and cordon one node in the pair. Shift traffic using our smart router to partner and warm caches.
3) Drain non-hot traffic off the target node (gradual). Keep lightweight inference in flight to ensure graceful degradation.
4) Install driver bundle and run smoke tests (healthchecks + 5 synthetic inference calls).
5) Run 10-minute golden tests: latency distribution check, 1k inference sampling for correctness.
6) If green, uncordon and let traffic re-flow. Observe for 30 minutes.
7) Repeat for partner node.
8) If any step fails, follow rollback: re-install previous driver, uncordon failed partner, failover traffic back to previous stable node, escalate (page infra-lead).

Rollback/on-failure summary
- Abort criteria: >2.5% 5xxs for 10 continuous minutes OR failure of golden test (95% of sample responses > 0.95 similarity threshold to baseline).
- Immediate steps: failback traffic, reinstall prior driver bundle, re-run smoke tests. Capture traces and open a postmortem ticket.

Post-window checks
- Validate model output fidelity for top-10 routes (Maya) — run regression checks.
- Confirm KV warm-up hit rate returned to pre-maintenance levels within 2 hours.
- Check cost delta (inefficient batching causing extra tokens) — expect <5% cost bump; file follow-up if >5%.
- Close loop with CS on customer impact reports and update SLA incident board if necessary.

Quick command checklist (ops snippets)
- Mark pair: infractl node cordon --node node-123
- Drain: infractl node drain --node node-123 --grace 600 --exclude-priority=high
- Install: ssh root@node-123 'dpkg -i /tmp/nv-driver-525_1.deb && systemctl restart gpu-service'
- Smoke test: infractl probe --node node-123 --profile golden-1000

Open questions / risks (short list)
- Is pairing sufficient for NVLink-dependent models? For certain models that span both nodes in a pair we may see stateful degradation; need to confirm with model owners.
- Driver regression with kernel X.Y.Z observed in staging on small number of tests — need extended canary on eu-west1 pilot.
- Does Dedicated routing need temporary capacity buffer created by borrowing from other regions (cross-region spill)? Legal/Compliance check pending for data residency.

Follow-ups and action items
- Diego: run extended pilot with 24h warmup synthetic traffic against eu-west1 pilot cluster (due 2026-05-12).
- Maya: prepare regression suite list for top-10 routes (due 2026-05-14).
- Priya: coordinate customer notifications and special handling list (due 2026-05-13).
- Tomas: create emergency rollback automation PR and attach to GitHub #902 (due 2026-05-11).

Notes to self
- Keep this doc as the lightweight ops-run notes. After the pilot, merge validated steps into the canonical infra runbook (confluence:infra/driver-upgrades-2026-Q2) and change status to final.
- Expect deviations; record them inline during the run for the postmortem.

Appendix: simple impact matrix (text table)
Region | GPUs total | Reserved | Max removal | Notes
eu-west1 | 320 | 64 | 12% | Pilot cluster, use as canary
us-west1 | 560 | 140 | 18% | Spread across two colos
us-east1 | 480 | 120 | 15% | Nighttime window preferred
ap-southeast1 | 120 | 24 | 6% | Lowest traffic, last to run

End of doc
